split_reasoning: Test plans and detailed test cases or scripts are different deliverables, even though both support testing.

parts.text: Design a test plan for a software change or release.
parts.type_reasoning: A completed test plan is a distinct artifact used by the test team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A plan for one release or change is reviewed and used as a whole.
parts.work_item: one test plan
parts.start: requirements and scope for the change or release are available
parts.end: test plan is prepared and shared for review or use

parts.text: Design test scenarios, scripts, or procedures for software functionality.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces documented test designs that testers can execute.
parts.unit_reasoning: A related set of cases or scripts is handed over for a feature or test objective.
parts.work_item: one feature-level set of test cases or scripts
parts.start: feature requirements or test objectives are available
parts.end: cases or scripts are ready for review and execution

notes: The boundary between a plan and detailed cases varies by team; time shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: One activity: testing a system change before it goes live.

parts.text: Execute tests on a system modification and report whether it is ready for implementation.
parts.type_reasoning: Each test cycle ends in recorded results and a go/no-go recommendation others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Testing is handed over per change or release as a completed test cycle with results and sign-off.
parts.work_item: one system modification tested (one test cycle)
parts.start: change deployed to the test environment and assigned for testing
parts.end: test results recorded and change signed off or returned with defects

split_reasoning: One activity: building test suites; the listed areas (database, regression, negative, retest, usability) are kinds of coverage for the same deliverable.

parts.text: Develop a test suite covering a given area such as regression, negative testing, database impacts, bug retests, or usability.
parts.type_reasoning: Each suite is a distinct deliverable that is reviewed and then executed by testers.
parts.unit_reasoning: Suites are built and handed over per area and release, then reviewed before use.
parts.work_item: one test suite for one testing area of a release
parts.start: testing area and scope assigned
parts.end: suite written, reviewed, and added to the test repository

notes: Close to 14638; 'testing programs' could also mean automated suites, which overlap 14659.

split_reasoning: Documenting a defect and reporting it to developers is one workflow step producing one bug report.

parts.text: Write up a defect in the bug tracking system and assign or report it to the developers.
parts.type_reasoning: Each defect report is a distinct written deliverable developers act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The bug ticket is the unit that enters the developers' queue.
parts.work_item: one defect report filed in the bug tracker
parts.start: defect observed during testing
parts.end: ticket filed with steps to reproduce, severity, and evidence, and assigned to a developer

notes: 14642 includes identifying and analyzing the problem, which shares the documentation step with this statement.

split_reasoning: One activity: identifying and analyzing a problem; function, output, screen, and content are kinds of the same item.

parts.text: Identify a problem with program function, output, screen, or content, analyze it, and document it.
parts.type_reasoning: Each problem ends in a documented finding others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Problems are tracked one at a time as analyzed findings.
parts.work_item: one program problem identified, analyzed, and documented
parts.start: unexpected behavior noticed during testing or review
parts.end: problem reproduced, characterized, and documented

notes: Substantial overlap with 14641; the analysis step distinguishes this one.

split_reasoning: Monitoring bug resolution is ongoing and yields two kinds of item: following up and closing out individual fixed defects, and periodic tracking reports.

parts.text: Follow up on a defect marked fixed: check its status, verify the fix, and close or reopen it.
parts.type_reasoning: Each defect follow-up ends in a status change others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Defects are closed out one ticket at a time.
parts.work_item: one resolved defect verified and closed or reopened
parts.start: developer marks the defect fixed
parts.end: ticket closed or reopened with a note

parts.text: Produce a periodic defect-resolution status report tracking open, fixed, and closed bugs.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a report that managers read and act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The status report is what is sent to the team each week or sprint.
parts.work_item: one defect status report (weekly or per sprint)
parts.start: pull of current defect data from the tracker
parts.end: report with counts, trends, and blockers sent to the project team

notes: Time shares are a judgment; part a overlaps the bug retests named in 14640.

split_reasoning: Creating a known-defects database is an occasional setup job, while maintaining it is ongoing curation, so the two are split.

parts.text: Set up a database or tracker project for known test defects.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a working database that the team relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The database is set up and handed over once per product or project.
parts.work_item: one known-defects database set up
parts.start: need for a defect repository agreed
parts.end: database configured with fields and workflows and opened to the team

parts.text: Update and clean up the known-defects database: merge duplicates, update statuses, and add workarounds.
parts.type_reasoning: Maintenance is ongoing, so it is recast into periodic curation batches, which others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Curation is typically done in periodic passes, for example before a release or each sprint.
parts.work_item: one curation pass over the known-defects database
parts.start: scheduled review or release milestone
parts.end: records updated, duplicates merged, and known-issues list current
parts.checked_by: QA lead / support and development teams

notes: Day-to-day defect entry belongs to 14641; this coding treats maintenance as curation.

split_reasoning: One activity: planning testing for a project; schedules and strategies are parts of the same planning deliverable.

parts.text: Prepare the test strategy and schedule for a project or release according to its scope and delivery dates.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a strategy and schedule document that managers approve and follow.
parts.unit_reasoning: Test strategy and schedule are signed off per project or release.
parts.work_item: one test strategy and schedule for a project or release
parts.start: project scope and delivery dates received
parts.end: strategy and schedule approved by project stakeholders

notes: Overlaps with test plans in 14638, which often contain the schedule.

split_reasoning: The listed subjects are different inputs to the same product design review interaction.

parts.text: Participate in a product design review and provide testing-related input.
parts.type_reasoning: The target is participation and discussion in a live review.

notes: Any separately prepared review document is not specified by the target.

split_reasoning: One activity: reviewing a document; accuracy, compliance, completeness, and risk are criteria for the same review.

parts.text: Review a software document for technical accuracy, compliance, completeness, and risks, and return findings.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces a findings list or sign-off the author relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Reviews are assigned and returned per document.
parts.work_item: one software document reviewed with findings
parts.start: document submitted for review
parts.end: findings returned or document approved

split_reasoning: One activity: writing up test procedures.

parts.text: Write up a test procedure in enough detail that it can be repeated and meets documentation standards.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a procedure document others follow and auditors may check.
parts.unit_reasoning: Procedures are documented and approved one at a time or per test area.
parts.work_item: one test procedure documented
parts.start: test procedure designed or run
parts.end: procedure document reviewed and stored in the test repository

split_reasoning: One activity: defining quality or release-readiness standards; standards, methods, and procedures are forms of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Develop or specify a quality standard, method, or release-readiness criteria.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a standard or criteria document that teams adopt.
parts.unit_reasoning: Standards and criteria are written and approved as documents.
parts.work_item: one quality standard or set of release-readiness criteria
parts.start: need for a standard or criteria identified
parts.end: document approved and published to the team

split_reasoning: One activity: keeping automated scripts current.

parts.text: Update automated test scripts to reflect product changes.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces updated scripts that run in the test pipeline and are code-reviewed.
parts.unit_reasoning: Script updates are committed as one change set per product change or sprint.
parts.work_item: one set of automated test scripts updated for a product change
parts.start: product change breaks or outdates scripts
parts.end: updated scripts reviewed, merged, and passing in the pipeline

split_reasoning: One activity: investigating an escalated customer problem.

parts.text: Investigate a customer problem referred by technical support and report the findings.
parts.type_reasoning: Each escalation ends in findings or a defect report that support relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Escalations arrive as tickets and are closed one at a time.
parts.work_item: one escalated customer problem investigated
parts.start: escalation ticket received from technical support
parts.end: problem reproduced or not, findings returned to support, and defect filed if needed

split_reasoning: Installing or maintaining testing tools is a different activity from using them to run tests.

parts.text: Install, configure, or upgrade a software testing tool.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a working tool installation the team relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tool installs and upgrades are handled as one change or ticket each.
parts.work_item: one testing tool installed or upgraded
parts.start: tool install or upgrade requested
parts.end: tool working and available to the team

parts.text: Use testing tools to run a test session and record the results.
parts.type_reasoning: Each test run produces results others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Test runs are logged and reported per execution cycle.
parts.work_item: one test run executed with results recorded
parts.start: test run scheduled or triggered
parts.end: results logged in the test management tool

split_reasoning: Feedback is given both as written recommendations and in informal discussion with developers, which are different activities.

parts.text: Write usability and functionality feedback and recommendations on a build for developers.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces written feedback developers act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Feedback is sent per build or feature, as a note or set of tickets.
parts.work_item: one written feedback note on a build or feature
parts.start: build or feature evaluated
parts.end: feedback and recommendations sent to developers

parts.text: Discuss usability and functionality with developers in meetings or informal conversation.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the conversation; nothing a colleague would check is produced.

notes: The split between written and spoken feedback is a judgment.

split_reasoning: Performance monitoring is continuous, but its actionable outputs are individual performance issues investigated.

parts.text: Investigate a performance issue identified through program monitoring.
parts.type_reasoning: Each identified issue produces findings or an escalation that others can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: An observed performance issue is investigated and communicated as a unit.
parts.work_item: one monitored performance issue investigated
parts.start: monitoring reveals a performance anomaly or threshold breach
parts.end: findings are recorded and the issue is closed or escalated
parts.checked_by: developers and operations or test lead

notes: Some workplaces also produce periodic performance summaries; the target does not specify a reporting cadence.

split_reasoning: One activity: compatibility testing; programs, hardware, operating systems, and networks are kinds of environments for the same test.

parts.text: Run compatibility tests of a build across target programs, hardware, operating systems, or network environments.
parts.type_reasoning: Each cycle produces a compatibility results matrix others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Compatibility testing is reported per build across its configuration matrix.
parts.work_item: one compatibility test cycle for a build
parts.start: build and configuration matrix ready
parts.end: compatibility results recorded and issues filed

notes: Hardware-based compatibility testing may involve some hands-on setup.

split_reasoning: One activity: building a production-like test environment.

parts.text: Install and configure a recreation of the production environment for performance testing.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a working environment that testers rely on; today this is mostly done on virtual or cloud infrastructure at a computer.
parts.unit_reasoning: Environments are requested and handed over one at a time.
parts.work_item: one test environment built to mirror production
parts.start: environment request with production specification
parts.end: environment configured, verified, and handed to testers

notes: Where physical servers must be racked or cabled, a small physical part could be split off.

split_reasoning: One activity, diagnosing field problems, done in two places: in live sessions with field staff or customers, and afterwards when writing up the diagnosis and recommendations.

parts.text: Diagnose a problem in a live call or session with field staff or a customer.
parts.type_reasoning: The diagnostic work is done while the customer or field staff member is on the line.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each live session works through one reported problem.
parts.work_item: one problem diagnosed during a live session with field staff or a customer
parts.start: session begins with the problem described
parts.end: likely cause identified and next steps agreed
parts.checked_by: the customer or field staff member

parts.text: Write up the diagnosis and recommended solutions after working with field staff or customers.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a written recommendation others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The diagnosis and recommendation are sent per problem.
parts.work_item: one written diagnosis and recommended solution
parts.start: live session or field report ends
parts.end: recommendation sent to field staff, customer, or developers

notes: Whether live sessions count as LIVE_SERVICE or INTERPERSONAL is debatable.

split_reasoning: One activity: checking a program against standards and recommending fixes.

parts.text: Check a program against standards and recommend modifications to bring it into compliance.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a findings list with recommended changes that developers act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Compliance checks are done and reported per program or build.
parts.work_item: one standards-compliance review of a program with recommendations
parts.start: program or build submitted for compliance check
parts.end: deviations and suggested changes sent to developers

split_reasoning: One activity: building testing tools; designing and developing are steps of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Design and build an automated testing tool or framework component.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces working code that testers rely on and that is code-reviewed.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tools are built and merged as a feature or component.
parts.work_item: one automated testing tool or framework component
parts.start: tool need or specification agreed
parts.end: tool reviewed, merged, and in use by the team

split_reasoning: Coordinating outside testing involves setting up a test round, compiling its results, and live coordination with users or vendors, which are different activities.

parts.unit_reasoning: Outside testing is organized per round or release.
parts.work_item: one user or third-party test round organized

parts.end: participants briefed with scripts, schedule, and access

parts.text: Compile the results of a user or third-party test round into a findings report.

parts.text: Coordinate with users or third-party testers during testing through meetings and check-ins.

split_reasoning: One activity: first-pass debugging; config files, logs, and code are alternative inputs for the same diagnosis.

parts.text: Review configuration files, logs, or code to find the likely source of a failure.
parts.type_reasoning: Each investigation ends in a root-cause note on the ticket that developers rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Initial debugging is done and recorded per defect.

split_reasoning: Visiting a beta site and evaluating performance there are connected parts of one on-site evaluation.

parts.type_reasoning: The site evaluation produces findings that the product team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: Findings from one site visit are normally communicated together.

parts.start: a beta site and evaluation objectives are identified
parts.end: site observations and performance findings are documented or shared

split_reasoning: One activity: evaluating tools and giving a recommendation.

parts.text: Evaluate testing or bug tracking software and recommend whether to adopt it.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a recommendation that managers decide on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Evaluations are done and reported per tool or tool selection.
